dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:1101.text: To follow. Formed from 辵, with abbreviated 𡐦 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1102.text: A manner of walking. Formed from 辵, with 巿 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1103.text: To go. Formed from 辵, with 王 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn commentary says: “Do not deceive me.”

shuowen:1104.text: To go. Formed from 辵, with 折 indicating the sound. Read like 誓.

shuowen:1105.text: To go. Formed from 辵, with 且 indicating the sound. 䢐 is a word of Qi.

shuowen:1106.text: To follow. Formed from 辵, with 术 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1107.text: To follow. Formed from 辵, with 尊 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1108.text: To go to. Formed from 辵, with 啻 indicating the sound. 適 is a word of Song and Lu.

shuowen:1109.text: To cross or pass. Formed from 辵, with 咼 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1110.text: To become accustomed. Formed from 辵, with 貫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1111.text: Familiarity bordering on disrespect, 媟䢱. Formed from 辵, with 𧷏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1112.text: To ascend. Formed from 辵, with abbreviated 閵 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1113.text: To approach or attain. Formed from 辵, with 告 indicating the sound. Tan Chang explains: 造 means a superior scholar.

shuowen:1114.text: To cross forward. Formed from 辵, with 俞 indicating the sound. The Book of Zhou says: “Do not dare recklessly to overstep.”

shuowen:1115.text: To reach, overtake or catch up with someone or something. Formed from 辵, with 眔 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1116.text: To reach or catch up with, the same as 遝. Formed from 辵, with 合 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1117.text: 迮迮: to rise. Formed from 辵, with abbreviated 作 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1118.text: To cross or move obliquely, especially in alternating or intersecting paths. Formed from 辵, with 昔 indicating the sound. [Duan argues that the received 迹逪 should instead read 䢒逪.]

shuowen:1119.text: To go back and forth frequently. Formed from 辵, with 耑 indicating the sound. The Changes says: “Go swiftly about the matter.”

shuowen:1120.text: Swift. Formed from 辵, with 束 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1121.text: Swift. Formed from 辵, with 卂 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1122.text: Swift. Formed from 辵, with 𠯑 indicating the sound. Pronounced the same as 括.

shuowen:1123.text: To meet. Formed from 辵, with 屰 indicating the sound. East of the pass they say 逆; west of the pass, 迎.

shuowen:1124.text: To meet. Formed from 辵, with 卬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1125.text: To meet or assemble. Formed from 辵, with 交 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1126.text: To encounter. Formed from 辵, with 禺 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1127.text: To encounter. Formed from 辵, with 曹 indicating the sound. Another explanation: to travel in a continuous line.

shuowen:1128.text: To encounter. Formed from 辵, with 冓 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1129.text: To encounter. Formed from 辵, with abbreviated 峯 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1130.text: To meet and be startled. Formed from 辵 and 㖾; 㖾 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:1131.text: A way or guidance. Formed from 辵, with 由 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1132.text: To change or replace in turn. Formed from 辵, with 虒 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1133.text: To reach through. Formed from 辵, with 甬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1134.text: To move. Formed from 辵, with 止 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1135.text: To change one's location. Formed from 辵, with 多 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1136.text: To ascend. Formed from 辵, with 𠨧 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1137.text: To move or transfer. Formed from 辵, with 軍 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1138.text: To move away. Another explanation: to escape. Formed from 辵, with 盾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1139.text: To withdraw or escape. Formed from 辵, with 孫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1140.text: To return. Formed from 辵 and 反; 反 also indicates the sound. The Book of Shang says: “Zu Jia returned.”

shuowen:1141.text: To return. Formed from 辵, with 瞏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1142.text: To dispatch. Formed from 辵 and 巽: 巽 sends it away; 巽 also indicates the sound. Another explanation: 選 means to choose.

shuowen:1143.text: To send away. Formed from 辵 and abbreviated 㑞.

shuowen:1144.text: To release or send off. Formed from 辵, with 𠳋 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1145.text: To walk in a winding or continuous course, described as 邐邐. Formed from 辵, with 麗 indicating the sound. [The precise descriptive sense is uncertain.]

shuowen:1146.text: 唐逮: to reach. Formed from 辵, with 隶 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1147.text: To walk slowly. Formed from 辵, with 犀 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Traveling the road slowly.”

shuowen:1148.text: Slow. Formed from 辵, with 黎 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1149.text: To depart. Formed from 辵, with 帶 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1150.text: A manner of walking. Formed from 辵, with 𣶒 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1151.text: Not to walk. Formed from 辵, with 𩣷 indicating the sound. Read like 住.

shuowen:1152.text: To stop. Formed from 辵, with 豆 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1153.text: To walk crookedly. Formed from 辵, with 只 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1154.text: 逶迆: the appearance of going obliquely away. Formed from 辵, with 委 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1155.text: To travel obliquely. Formed from 辵, with 也 indicating the sound. The Book of Xia says: “Winding east and north, it joins at Hui.”

shuowen:1156.text: To turn aside and avoid. Formed from 辵, with 矞 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1157.text: To turn aside. Formed from 辵, with 辟 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1158.text: To separate or depart. Formed from 辵, with 韋 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1159.text: To walk with difficulty. Formed from 辵, with 㷠 indicating the sound. The Changes says: “Going onward brings difficulty.”

shuowen:1160.text: To return. Formed from 辵, with 夋 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1161.text: To refuse angrily to advance. Formed from 辵, with 氐 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1162.text: To travel without meeting one another. Formed from 辵, with 羍 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Leaping and wandering.”

shuowen:1163.text: To walk cautiously, 逯逯. Formed from 辵, with 录 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1164.text: 迵 means to alternate, 迭. Formed from 辵, with 同 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1165.text: To alternate or replace in turn. Formed from 辵, with 失 indicating the sound. Another explanation: to reach, 达.

shuowen:1166.text: To be confused. Formed from 辵, with 米 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1167.text: Originally, a carriage drawn or pulled along by a person, related to the old form of 輦; later, things joined in an unbroken sequence. Formed from 辵 and 車. [Duan argues the transmitted gloss 員連 is corrupt for 負車.]

shuowen:1168.text: To collect or gather. Formed from 辵, with 求 indicating the sound. The Book of Yu says: “Seek widely to complete the achievements.” A separate saying states: “A hostile or ill-matched partner is called 逑.” This latter use corresponds to 仇 in a parallel textual tradition.

shuowen:1169.text: To defeat or ruin, 𣀩. Formed from 辵, with 貝 indicating the sound. The Book of Zhou says: “We rise to receive its defeat.”

shuowen:1170.text: To escape. Formed from 辵, with 官 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1171.text: To escape. Formed from 辵 and 豚.

shuowen:1172.text: To flee. Formed from 辵, with 甫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1173.text: To lose. Formed from 辵, with 䝿 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1174.text: To perish or go away. Formed from 辵, with 㒸 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1175.text: To flee. Formed from 辵, with 兆 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1176.text: To pursue. Formed from 辵, with 𠂤 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1177.text: To pursue. Formed from 辵 and abbreviated 豚.

shuowen:1178.text: To press upon. Formed from 辵, with 酉 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1179.text: To be near or attached. Formed from 辵, with 斤 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1180.text: To compress, fold or draw together. Formed from 辵, with 巤 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1181.text: Near. Formed from 辵, with 白 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1182.text: Near. Formed from 辵, with 臸 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1183.text: Near. Formed from 辵, with 爾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1184.text: To stop gently or slightly. Formed from 辵, with 曷 indicating the sound. Read like 蝎, the mulberry insect.

shuowen:1185.text: To stop or block. Formed from 辵, with 庶 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1186.text: To obstruct, 遮䢭. Formed from 辵, with 羨 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1187.text: To bar the way, 迾. Jin and Zhao call it 迣. Formed from 辵, with 丗 indicating the sound. Read like 寘.

shuowen:1188.text: To obstruct. Formed from 辵, with 𠛱 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1189.text: To advance. Formed from 辵, with 干 indicating the sound. Read like 干.

shuowen:1190.text: To pass. Formed from 辵, with 侃 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1191.text: To continue or move in an unbroken succession. Formed from 辵, with 婁 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1192.text: To move forward with the face or head thrust out, as in a particular way of running or moving. Formed from 辵, with 巿 indicating the sound. Palace Attendant Jia offers readings like 㭘 or 郅. [Duan discusses a competing graph and the gloss 䢡走也.]

shuowen:1193.text: 𨔣互: to prevent passage. Formed from 辵, with 枷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1194.text: To cross or exceed. Formed from 辵, with 戉 indicating the sound. The Changes says: “Mixed, yet not exceeding bounds.”

shuowen:1195.text: To pass through. Formed from 辵, with 呈 indicating the sound. Chu calls rapid walking 逞. The Spring and Autumn commentary says: “Where would he not gratify his desires?”

shuowen:1196.text: Far. Formed from 辵, with 尞 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1197.text: Far. Formed from 辵, with 袁 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1198.text: Far. Formed from 辵, with 狄 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1199.text: Far. Formed from 辵, with 冋 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1200.text: Far. Formed from 辵, with 卓 indicating the sound. Another explanation: lame. Read like 棹 in 棹苕.
